#Uranium #Copper #Silver #Gold
11 NOVEMBER | ASIA BUYS THE DIP. THE RATE SHOCK REMAINS.

Gold and silver are bouncing after yesterday’s inflation-driven selloff. Asian equities also rallied as CoreWeave’s results helped restore confidence in AI spending. But a firm dollar and renewed Fed tightening expectations remain obstacles.

☢️ URANIUM
Yesterday’s NexGen call offered a useful signal: management reported continued strong interest and urgency from utilities worldwide, with no material change following the US election. Rook I construction remains on schedule and budget, according to the company.

My take: utility procurement deserves more attention than daily swings in uranium equities.

🔌 COPPER
China’s physical market remains tight. Latest reported SHFE stocks stand at just 33,848 tonnes—a three-year low—while the Yangshan import premium reached a record $230/t on Monday.

Funds have been reducing exposure while Chinese buyers face scarce available metal. Watch whether physical demand can support prices through the macro turbulence.

🥈 SILVER
Back above $53. Spot silver climbed 2.9% to $53.01, leading the precious-metals rebound. Encouraging buying after the selloff, but follow-through into Europe will matter.

🥇 GOLD
Spot gold recovered 0.6% to $4,057.33 after Tuesday’s near-3% decline. Markets are fully pricing a December Fed hike, keeping pressure on non-yielding bullion.

👀 TODAY’S TEST
Can Europe extend Asia’s recovery while the dollar stays firm?
I’m watching silver’s follow-through, Chinese copper premiums and uranium contracting signals.

Follow @Swedish_Uranium for the daily metals pulse.

People keep asking me what I think the market will do next. That’s one of the stupidest questions you can ask. Nobody knows what the market will do next.

What you can do is observe what’s happening right now. And to do that, you don’t need anyone’s help.

The $VIX is falling hard. Nasdaq volatility ($VXN) is falling hard. Oil prices are falling, and oil volatility is falling hard. These are all bullish signs.

It’s like asking when summer will arrive instead of observing that the days are getting longer, temperatures are rising, the snow is melting, and the trees are beginning to bloom.

You don’t need to predict the season. You just need to observe the signs of its arrival.

tweets.text:
The Democratic midterm sweep has raised valid questions about the AI data centre buildout. The reality is more nuanced than the recent market reaction suggests.

2027 capacity looks largely intact. Most projects scheduled to come online next year are already under construction and newly elected governors are not expected to disrupt work that has started. Hyperscaler capex forecasts for 2027 remain essentially unchanged.

The risk sits further out. Roughly 20% of planned US capacity for 2028 (about 5 GW) could slip into 2029, mainly in Texas and Ohio, as new permitting and utility rules are written. This creates a potential air pocket for parts of the supply chain in 2028, but it is a delay not a cancellation.

Power constraints and interconnection queues were already going to push some projects later. Politics is now an additional variable, not the sole driver.

The AI infrastructure cycle is being extended, it is not ending. For quality names with strong free cash flow, durable backlogs and pricing power, the recent selloff looks more like a sentiment reset than a fundamental one. It pays to be greedy when others are fearful.
